# Belenko Design Studio

> Barcelona-based hospitality interior design studio. We design restaurants, bars, cafés, hotels and beach clubs as complete business products — concept, interior, brand, guest experience, FF&E and opening. Founded 1999 · 200+ venues · 11 countries · projects in Europe and the United States.

Canonical site: https://www.belenko.design
Contact: office@belenko.design · +34 671 825 489 (WhatsApp) · Pl. de Lesseps, 6-7, 08023 Barcelona, Spain
Founder and principal: Denys Belenko (architect, M.Arch)

## What we do

Four engagement packages (details: https://www.belenko.design/#services):

- **Concept & Interior** — positioning, space planning, interior and lighting design, construction documentation. https://www.belenko.design/clients/proposal/concept-interior
- **Full-Service** — concept → design → FF&E procurement → construction administration → opening, one team and one point of accountability. https://www.belenko.design/clients/proposal/full-service
- **Brand & Guest Experience** — identity, menu structure, tableware, uniforms and service behaviour, launch and content. https://www.belenko.design/clients/proposal/brand-experience
- **Consulting / Audit** — location check before a lease, audit of an operating venue, second opinion on another studio's design. https://www.belenko.design/clients/proposal/consulting

Service pages by venue type: restaurant, bar, café, hotel design — https://www.belenko.design/services/restaurant-design and sibling pages.

## Who we work with

Restaurant groups, independent chef-driven restaurateurs, hotel and resort developers, investors and developers who need hospitality concepts built around commercial performance.

## Where we work

Headquarters in Barcelona, Spain. Portfolio on the site covers Spain, Turkey, Azerbaijan, Moldova, Ukraine and the United States (Sarasota, FL); the studio has completed 200+ projects in 11 countries overall.
United States: https://www.belenko.design/florida and https://www.belenko.design/california-hospitality-design. For U.S. projects we partner with a local architect of record and general contractor, manage the project remotely with site visits at key stages, and design to ADA requirements.

## Key facts

- Founded: 1999 (25+ years in hospitality design)
- Completed projects: 200+, in 11 countries, 538,000+ sq ft of designed venues
- In-house FF&E department: specification, sourcing, tenders, procurement, logistics, installation and site acceptance
- Languages: English, Spanish, Ukrainian, Russian
- Positioning: interior design as a business tool — venues designed to raise the average check, table turnover and guest return rate

## Design philosophy

"We don't design interiors — we design how the guest feels." Every venue is a script: where the guest pauses, what they see first, where the light falls, how they settle in, what they feel as they leave. Ideas are driven by positioning rather than trends; materials that age well (wood, stone, brick, metal), warm layered light, handcrafted detail, and a brand the guest carries with them.

## Typical process and timing

Concept and positioning 3–4 weeks → design package 10–14 weeks → construction 4–7 months depending on the site. Most restaurants open 8–12 months after the first meeting. Fees are fixed per project after a first consultation; three engagement models (concept-and-interior, full-service, consulting by the day).

## FAQ

**Do you work in the United States?** Yes — Florida, California, Texas and New York, with a completed project in Sarasota, FL; local architect of record and GC partnership, remote project management, site visits at key stages.

**How much does restaurant interior design cost?** It depends on scope, venue size and location; every project receives a fixed-fee proposal after the first consultation.

**How long does a restaurant design project take?** Typically 8–12 months from first meeting to opening (design 3–4 months, construction 4–7 months).

**Can you audit an existing restaurant?** Yes — location assessment before a lease, audit of an operating venue, or a second opinion on another studio's design, on site or remotely.

**Do you handle furniture and equipment?** Yes — in-house FF&E: specification, sourcing, procurement, logistics and installation control.
